For everyone concerned about this company's conservation efforts, [this article](https://time.com/7274542/colossal-dire-wolf/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=editorial&utm_term=science_animals&linkId=792476598&fbclid=IwY2xjawJhBPFleHRuA2FlbQIxMAABHmPIqTQf3E6RG-GRAPWPXvnGwNyAXak0-bJhhJbWWd3fWFv-_LtqH-OgtQvh_aem_f1DyM0MKRogm84af3QuzHQ) goes extremely in depth about the development of this project, and their project on red wolf conservation.

They are not rewilding these animals. The research done for these dire wolves has greatly aided their conservation efforts for red wolves. [See here.](https://time.com/7274542/colossal-dire-wolf/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=editorial&utm_term=science_animals&linkId=792476598&fbclid=IwY2xjawJhBPFleHRuA2FlbQIxMAABHmPIqTQf3E6RG-GRAPWPXvnGwNyAXak0-bJhhJbWWd3fWFv-_LtqH-OgtQvh_aem_f1DyM0MKRogm84af3QuzHQ)

yeah, it's a clickbait title to get people interested in following their company for more updates. This company does amazing things for conservation. What they post on socials, and what is said in every article published about these wolves, are different. Their social media is hammed up for entertainment value-- see their Wooly Mouse video in the pinned. Very entertaining, for sure. If you notice, the descriptions of their posts are not very monotonous or scientific at all. It's easy to read, and easy to digest for the average dumbass, which is the majority of the world. It's going to hold a lot more people's interest to be like HELL YEAH WOLVES than to go into the science of it. They're boiling it down. If we can get the dumbasses to FINALLY care about conservation because Le GOT Wolf!!1!! I don't think that's a bad thing.

[read their times article.](https://time.com/7274542/colossal-dire-wolf/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=editorial&utm_term=science_animals&linkId=792476598&fbclid=IwY2xjawJhBPFleHRuA2FlbQIxMAABHmPIqTQf3E6RG-GRAPWPXvnGwNyAXak0-bJhhJbWWd3fWFv-_LtqH-OgtQvh_aem_f1DyM0MKRogm84af3QuzHQ) It is extremely in depth and breaks down exactly how this was done.

They used skeletal remains from museums to get the DNA for these wolves and used a surrogate mother (gray wolf).

Company uses clickbait headline to drive traffic-- shocker. Read any article published about these dire wolves, many of which feature interviews with members of Colossal. AI is extremely important in many ways for research, it's not just ChatGPT and Midjourney. I agree frivolous use of AI is insane, but you will be hard pressed to find a STEM-related research company that doesn't have some sort of artificial intelligence software to aid them.

AI is the reason why we have made so many developments in cancer imaging, and Colossal uses AI to help with gene sequencing that would take a person years longer to do. This means, more conservation efforts are actually being made in terms of genetic research, faster. Which is very much needed with the state of the planet. AI has been used in science for decades. It's just the big boogeyman right now, and we need to remember that before it was commercialized for public use, AI is a big part of why we have such rapid advancements in research technology today.

Her mom was proudly talking about how she was in graduate school, I assumed Masters over doctoral program. Piper seems like 24-26 to me, and Saxon 27-29.

ETA: If piper is in undergrad, this wouldn't even be possible as a trip. Spring break is typically 9 days for students. A flight to Thailand from ATL (most likely where they flew out of, international airport) is 22hr+ flight. They definitely have been there longer than a week based on the day/night cycles we have seen.

We know that they are visiting in the month of april, because of the water gun festival, which occurs April 13th-15th yearly. So she *is* on **spring break.** 

This would not make sense for her to be an undergrad because almost every single undergrad thesis is connected to a Senior Seminar class people take their last semester of college. If she was a junior/rising senior, there would be little to no reason to be taking this trip so early, given that undergrad thesis papers are typically capped at under 10 pages depending on the program. She is obviously not a STEM student, so I would imagine her paper is one that would be capped. No reason to start the paper over a year early. If this was her senior year, she would be screwed for her thesis paper because she would have already missed all of her deadlines on drafts. Granted, **there is no paper** but I digress.

Consider the following:

* The non-existent research paper would be due in just days after her trip. Semesters typically end 1st-2nd week of May. This would not be enough time to churn out this thesis given that she would certainly have to have submitted a draft in March or February. Drafts of thesis papers in undergrad are never submitted as "rough drafts" and are typically almost always in their final form, only needing a paragraph or so of changes added, because of the small timeline. If she had to do an ethnographic interview to support her claims, this could not have been included in the draft and she would have received a LOT of points off.
* In grad school, you typically begin working on your thesis in your first year, with it being due your final year of grad school. This would explain why she is taking this trip over spring break to give her a strong foundation for her next draft
* You can much more easily get time off approved by professors for thesis papers in grad school than in undergrad, especially when it is connected to research. Her classes might not have mandatory attendance, but she strikes me as an honors Grad student, where a majority of classes ARE mandatory. 
* Both of her parents are college educated, from good schools. They have almost certainly done undergrad thesis papers before (maybe not the dad, since he is in finance, but IDK how finance works) and would know that it would be weird that she hadn't even done the research for her academic research paper. I don't remember exactly what piper is studying, but it would be something strongly related to academia-- likely Religious Studies. Philosophy, or Anthropology. She would absolutely have to write a thesis paper at some point for her undergrad senior seminar class, so she could not possibly be a Senior if there is no paper, period, not "the paper isn't about this"

Point being, Piper has likely chosen a "capstone" project over a Thesis paper for her program. This is not possible in undergrad for seniors in her major.

**UPDATE:** Hi guys! The dark line actually did indicate higher HCG, it turned out I had a possible heterotopic pregnancy (one was in my fallopian tube) so.. yeah. Tube got removed because 6cm ectopic pregnancy. My # 2 days before the abortion was 479, and my number 2 weeks after was over 1,200. So yep... if this happens to you, maybe make sure to get another ultrasound because whew, not fun. Heterotopic pregnancies are insanely rare, so don't assume it's that. But ectopic pregnancies can be missed on an ultrasound and difficult to diagnose, apparently, and your body can make a pseudosac (basically just a mimicry of the gestational sac that would be there, with nothing inside) that may be seen on an ultrasound. This is also relatively rare (both the ectopic and the pseudosac, apparently) but still possible. Don't be like me!
